experiments.title: Constructive-only vs capability-only vs typed effect-time admission
experiments.purpose: Test whether forbidding direct destructive primitives, or adding only a capability check, is sufficient to prevent unsafe external effect commits when closure, source epoch, selector state, revocation and recoverability can independently be invalid.
oracle_commit_requirements: no direct model-constructible destructive protected-state transition
experiments.distribution_note: Hazard probabilities were selected for broad mechanism coverage only. Rates are not production priors or FRANK risk estimates.
interpretation: The strong hypothesis 'remove destructive primitives and the agent is safe' is contradicted in this constructed state-transition family.
A host capability check alone is also insufficient when the authority is applied against stale, misselected, revoked or unrecoverable state.
All eight C9 effect-admission predicates are individually load-bearing in this generated family because dropping any one admits oracle-unsafe commits.
Zero mismatches for the complete gate are a property-test result against the declared oracle, not a formal proof that the real compiler/runtime/OS mediation is complete.
experiments.next_falsifier: Run the same contract through real WASI/Wasmtime or equivalent capability sandbox plus Python/Bash/Rust/C/WASM child processes, FFI, filesystem/database targets, crash/restart and prompt-injection cases; measure normal programming utility simultaneously.
